clue.text: A coin is distributed capital

indicators.note: coins handed out are scattered, so these letters are spread into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A coin is spread around, as money is in circulation.
explanation.walkthrough: The first two words and 'is' read as a sentence about money; only 'distributed' tells you to rearrange them.
explanation.definitionFit: Nicosia is the capital city of Cyprus.

clue.text: Functioning doubles borne by a hotel-island that appears in Genesis

definitions.text: Functioning doubles borne by a hotel-island that appears in Genesis

indicators.note: in a down entry the reversed word rides on top of the rest
doubles back, so the word is turned round

parts.note: on means working, functioning
taken as written
Sark is one of the Channel Islands

explanation.surface: Animals in pairs carried by a floating hotel in the Bible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doubles' also reads as the animals that went in two by two, which makes the whole clue a description of the vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: The ark of Genesis held pairs of every animal, a floating lodging that served as an island in the flood.

clue.text: A dove's call is lower in Scotland

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the soft murmur of a dove
second meaning: a lower is something that lows, a cow

explanation.walkthrough: 'Lower' reads as 'further down'; it is one who lows, i.e. a cow.
explanation.definitionFit: Doves make a soft cooing noise, and Scots dialect spells cow this way.

clue.text: Puzzling originator in Cologne is Tesla — or is it Einstein?

parts.note: cologne is a scent
the setter, who creates the puzzle, is I
taken as written
T is the symbol for the tesla, the SI unit of magnetic flux density

explanation.surface: A baffling inventor in the German city of Cologne is Tesla, or perhaps Einstein.
explanation.walkthrough: Cologne looks like the city, but it is eau de cologne. The question mark marks Einstein as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Einstein was a physicist, so he is an example of a researcher in the sciences.

clue.text: Do this to sailor, bishop and vicar that is carrying astatine

definitions.text: Do this to sailor, bishop and vicar that is carrying astatine

parts.note: AB, able-bodied seaman
REV, short for Reverend

indicators.note: the that-is letters hold the astatine symbol inside

parts.note: IE, id est
AT is the chemical symbol for astatine

explanation.surface: An instruction to shorten a string of titles, so the words become their short forms.
explanation.walkthrough: Each item is replaced by its short form, which is exactly what the clue tells you to do.
explanation.definitionFit: To shorten words to a few letters, such as REV for Reverend, is to contract them.

clue.text: Cricket match on well-tended ground that's used for trials

parts.note: a Test is an international cricket match
a bed is a cultivated patch of garden

explanation.surface: A cricket match is played on a carefully kept pitch, the kind used for trial games.
explanation.walkthrough: A Test is a full international cricket match, lasting up to five days.
explanation.definitionFit: A testbed is an environment or platform set up for experiments on new equipment or ideas.

clue.text: Chops branch up

indicators.note: in a down entry the word is read bottom to top

parts.note: a part, a division of something

explanation.surface: Cuts a branch above.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chops' looks like a verb; it is slang for the mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: Trap and chops are both slang for the mouth, as in 'shut your trap'.

clue.text: Kiss turning on son, 29?

indicators.note: the son letter is attached after
the letters are churned into a new order

parts.note: snog is British slang for a long kiss

explanation.surface: A kiss turns on a boy, giving examples of 29.
explanation.walkthrough: 29 is BALLADS; the question mark shows they are examples of songs. To snog is British slang for kissing passionately.
explanation.definitionFit: Ballads are a kind of song, so the plural answer covers them.

clue.text: Thorny subject of Blair's initial meandering discourse with his partner in crime

indicators.note: the first letter of the word

parts.note: Tony Blair's initial is the first letter of his name
a ramble is rambling talk
George W. Bush, Tony Blair's ally over the Iraq war

explanation.surface: Tony Blair's rambling remarks with his ally make a prickly topic.
explanation.walkthrough: Blair and Bush led the 2003 invasion of Iraq, which critics called a crime.
explanation.definitionFit: A bramble bush is a prickly shrub, literally a thorny thing.

clue.text: Tedious academic quick to belt out Latin

parts.note: DR, a doctor

indicators.note: to throw out, so the Latin letter is removed

parts.note: early, as in a quick or prompt reply

explanation.surface: A boring professor is quick to sing out in Latin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Belt out' wants to mean sing loudly; here it means expel.
explanation.definitionFit: Dreary means dull and monotonous, which is another way of saying boring.

clue.text: One associated with trouble involving egg mayonnaise?

indicators.note: placed alongside, so the pieces are joined end to end
the trouble word surrounds the egg letter, which sits inside it

parts.note: to ail is to trouble, as in 'what ails you?'
an egg is round, shaped like the letter O
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone linked with a problem involving egg mayonnaise, perhaps food poisoning.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark shows the definition is by example: aioli is one kind of mayonnaise.
explanation.definitionFit: Aioli is a garlic-flavoured mayonnaise from Provence, so it is an instance of the sauce.

clue.text: Put underwear on at home then move to and fro — good idea!

indicators.note: the underwear is put on top of, i.e. before, what follows

parts.note: a bra is an item of underwear
in means at home, as in 'staying in'
to wave is to move back and forth

explanation.surface: Dressing in underwear at home and swaying about is hailed as a great plan.
explanation.definitionFit: A brainwave is a sudden clever inspiration.

clue.text: Park-keeper following devout individual who's from elsewhere

indicators.note: the park-keeper's word comes after the devout individual

parts.note: a saint, abbreviated ST
a ranger looks after a park or forest

explanation.surface: A park warden tails a pious person who is not from round here.
explanation.definitionFit: A stranger is an outsider, someone not known locally.

clue.text: Enterprising recluse made mincemeat with four bananas

indicators.note: chopped up finely, so the letters are rearranged
crazy, another call to jumble the letters

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A hermit cooked mince pies with four bananas.
explanation.definitionFit: Resourceful means good at finding quick, clever ways to overcome difficulties.

clue.text: Line formed when odd characters are ejected from gin shop/taproom

indicators.note: throwing out the first, third and fifth letters leaves the even ones

parts.note: taken as written; only its even letters are kept
a taproom is a bar

explanation.surface: Strange folk are thrown out of a gin palace, forming a queue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Odd characters' sounds like eccentric customers; here it means the letters in odd positions.
explanation.definitionFit: An isobar is a line on a weather map joining points of equal pressure.

clue.text: They cover hits by Underworld

indicators.note: next to, so the pieces are placed side by side

parts.note: to lamp is slang for to hit
Hades is the underworld of Greek myth

explanation.surface: Cover versions of songs by the band Underworld.
explanation.walkthrough: Underworld is also an electronic band, so 'cover' and 'hits' read as music.
explanation.definitionFit: Lampshades sit over light bulbs, shielding them.

clue.text: Barman removing earth from flowers in the entrance of inn

indicators.note: the earth letter is taken out of the flowers word

parts.note: roses are flowers
E is the abbreviation for earth in electrical wiring
taken as written

indicators.note: the first letter of the word, where you go in

parts.note: the first letter of inn

explanation.surface: A barman takes the soil off some flowers at the door of a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Barman' is a joke: Rossini wrote The Barber of Seville, so he is the man behind the Barber.
explanation.definitionFit: Gioachino Rossini composed the opera The Barber of Seville, making him its playful 'Barber-man'.

clue.text: Old German head of recruitment who may take up position at bank

definitions.text: who may take up position at bank

parts.note: the Angles were a Germanic people who settled in England

indicators.note: the first letter of the word

parts.note: its first letter

explanation.surface: An elderly German recruiting chief who might stand guard at a bank.
explanation.walkthrough: The bank sounds financial; it is a riverbank.
explanation.definitionFit: An angler fishes from a riverbank, taking up a spot there.

clue.text: Our arms once held this grown-up struggling to accept the ends of childhood innocence

indicators.note: the jumbled word takes the end letters inside
writhing, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the last letter of each of the two words

parts.note: the final letters of these two words

explanation.surface: An adult struggles to accept the end of childhood innocence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arms' looks like limbs holding a baby; it means firearms, which were once loaded with this.
explanation.definitionFit: Gunpowder was the explosive charge in old muskets and cannon.

clue.text: Registered name is 'Earl Z'!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: signed up, put on a register
second meaning, read as E then N rolled: E for earl, and an N turned on its side looks like Z

explanation.walkthrough: The second half is a reverse clue: split the answer into E, N and ROLLED, and an earl's E followed by a rolled-over N reads as 'Earl Z'.
explanation.definitionFit: Enrolled means officially entered on a list or register, as students are at a college.

clue.text: I disapprove of times one wears short skirt

indicators.note: the skirt goes around the one letter, as clothing goes round its wearer

parts.note: a tutu is a ballerina's short skirt
one of those two Ts
T is short for time; 'times' supplies two Ts

explanation.surface: Someone frowns on the way a person sometimes wears a mini-skirt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times' gives two Ts: one is worn inside the tutu, the other follows it.
explanation.definitionFit: Tut-tut is an exclamation of mild reproach, said to show disapproval.

clue.text: Writer given $1000 by posh, trendy publishers

parts.note: a pen is a writing instrument
G, a grand, is slang for a thousand dollars
U means upper-class
in means fashionable

explanation.surface: An author is paid a thousand dollars by smart, fashionable publishers.
explanation.definitionFit: Penguin is a well-known British publishing house, famous for paperbacks.

clue.text: Bus travelling north from city, heading for B&Q that's on the outskirts

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means read bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written
Ur was an ancient city of Mesopotamia

indicators.note: the first letter of the shop's name

parts.note: the first letter of the DIY chain's name

explanation.surface: A bus heading out of the city towards a B&Q out-of-town store.
explanation.walkthrough: B&Q is a British DIY chain whose large stores are often on the edge of towns.
explanation.definitionFit: A suburb is a residential district at the edge of a city.

clue.text: Relatives of diplomats with cold, uncovered flesh

parts.note: the UN, United Nations, is a body of diplomats

indicators.note: the outer letters are stripped off, leaving the inside of the word

parts.note: its middle letters are kept

explanation.surface: Diplomats' relations are left in the cold with bare skin.
explanation.definitionFit: Uncles are family members, brothers of a parent.

clue.text: A male nurse beside one's bottom put up fluid

indicators.note: in a down entry, raised means read bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written
EN, an enrolled nurse

indicators.note: the last letter, at the foot of the word

parts.note: the word one, whose bottom letter is wanted

explanation.surface: A male nurse next to someone's backside raises the fluid.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is about an awkward medical procedure, and the answer is just that.
explanation.definitionFit: An enema is liquid injected into the rectum to clean it out.

clue.text: Maybe Thomas the Tank Engine munches on the track

indicators.note: a track is a recording, so this is the words as heard

parts.note: chew chew, chewing over and over

explanation.surface: Thomas the Tank Engine chomps away on the railway line.
explanation.walkthrough: The railway track is a red herring; the track is a sound recording, which turns the chewing into a train's noise.
explanation.definitionFit: Choo-choo is a child's word for a steam train, of which Thomas is a famous example.

clue.text: Issue of Eagle, say, given to exhausted grandsons

indicators.note: the next piece is joined on

parts.note: EG, for example

indicators.note: emptied, so only the first and last letters remain

parts.note: the word with its middle emptied out, leaving its first and last letters

explanation.surface: An edition of the Eagle comic handed to worn-out grandsons.
explanation.walkthrough: The Eagle was a British boys' comic; the issue here is offspring of the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Eagles lay these, so they are the bird's offspring in its earliest form.

clue.text: Cuckoo defends gull both tail-less and unable to fly

indicators.note: crazy, so the letters are scrambled
each of the two words loses its last letter

parts.note: taken as written, minus its last letter
taken as written, minus its last letter

explanation.surface: A cuckoo protects a gull, both birds missing tails and grounded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cuckoo' looks like the bird among the other birds; it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An unfledged bird has not yet grown its flight feathers, so it cannot fly.

clue.text: Beelzebub was back

indicators.note: the word is read backwards

parts.note: lived, as in existed

explanation.surface: The demon has returned.
explanation.definitionFit: Beelzebub is a name for Satan or a chief demon.

clue.text: 6p for a big cheese

parts.note: VI is 6 in Roman numerals
p is the written abbreviation for a penny, kept as written

explanation.surface: Six pence for an important cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: A big cheese is an important person, a VIP.

clue.text: Music from party promotions

parts.note: a ball is a formal dance party
ads advertise, promoting products

explanation.surface: Tunes coming out of a party's publicity drive.
explanation.definitionFit: Ballads are songs, so they are a form of music.

clue.text: A piece of finest ripe dragonfruit or watermelon might be described thus

indicators.note: a run of letters is taken from inside these words

parts.note: the answer runs across the end of the first word, the whole second and the start of the third

explanation.surface: A slice of the best ripe tropical fruit or a melon could be called this.
explanation.walkthrough: The run spans the end of 'finest' through the start of 'dragonfruit'.
explanation.definitionFit: A watermelon's rind has dark green stripes, so the fruit is banded.
